title: Atletico take transfer spat public: ‘Don’t believe everything you see, especially if it’s related to Barca’
content:
Atletico Madrid have escalated their row with Barcelona over forward Julian Alvarez with a series of fake transfer rumour posts on social media, including pretending to offer Bad Bunny tickets in exchange for Lamine Yamal.

Atletico edited photos of Barcelona players Yamal, Pedri and Raphinha into Atletico shirts and accompanied these with the caption: “Don’t believe everything you see, especially if it’s related to Barca”

The Athletic reported on Thursday that Barcelona are in talks over a deal for Alvarez and are preparing a formal offer of around €100million ($116m; £87m). Atletico do not want to sell the 26-year-old Argentina international.

Atletico made the transfer saga public on Friday, firstly with a post on X that read: “In a few minutes, we will publish a statement about a relevant matter that is generating numerous pieces of disinformation.”

This was followed by a post with Barcelona forward Yamal edited into an Atletico shirt and captioned “Breaking, Here We Go” — a reference to the catchphrase of transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano.

Atletico’s post read: “We have sent a fax to Barcelona with our transfer offer: 4 tickets for tomorrow’s Bad Bunny concert, an annual subscription to ABC, and a bag of sunflower seeds. We eagerly await the response to prepare the ‘announce’.”

This post was followed by a similarly edited photo of Barcelona midfielder Gavi, accompanied by the caption: “For this second offer we’ve had a problem, we’ve run out of tickets for tomorrow’s concert, so we improve the previous proposal with 6 for the one on Sunday.”

A third photo of Barcelona forward Raphinha followed, with the caption: “And to complete the 3×1, we’ve got carried away and are going all out: the player arrives on loan for a season and in exchange we loan out Tom Ford and Smith with no option to buy. An offer impossible to refuse.”

On Instagram, Atletico posted the three edited photos with the caption: “And remember, it took us just five minutes to create this fake post. We live in an era where reality can be altered. Don’t believe everything you see, especially if it’s related to Barca.”

The Spanish club added a fourth post referencing Barcelona sporting director Deco. “Finally, we want to take this opportunity to categorically deny that we have made an offer to the sporting director of FC Barcelona to join our scouting team in the Brazilian market,” Atletico wrote.

A further post from Atletico read: “No, Atletico Madrid would never do anything like that. However, over the last few months we have been subjected to a smear campaign targeting one of our players.

“Self-serving leaks, ‘fake news’, constant disrespect, the Catalan side’s propaganda machine spinning tall tales, phone calls ahead of direct clashes… But of course, it would never occur to us to have the vice-president of the referees on our payroll or to resort to political favours to register players. RESPECT and VALUES.”

This last post was in reference to the so-called Negreira case — an investigation into payments totalling €8.4million made by Barcelona to former Spanish referees committee vice-president Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira.

A Barcelona court has since 2023 been investigating the payments, sent between 2001 and 2018 to companies connected to Negreira. Both Negreira and Barcelona have consistently denied wrongdoing.

Barcelona declined to comment when contacted by The Athletic.

Alvarez scored 20 goals in 49 appearances across all competitions during the 2025-26 season and is contracted to Atletico until 2030. He has been non-committal when asked about his Atletico future during the latter stages of the season.

“I couldn’t tell you; maybe yes, maybe no, you never know,” he told reporters in April when asked to confirm if he would still be at Atletico next season. “I’m very grateful to Atletico — the fans show me they love me, and I’m very happy here.”

Barcelona won a second consecutive La Liga title last season while Atletico finished fourth. Diego Simeone’s side did, however, knock Barcelona out of the Champions League at the quarter-final stage.

Analysis from Guillermo Rai

Atletico have finally snapped over Barcelona’s pursuit of Alvarez.

Earlier on Friday, Atletico sources spoke with The Athletic of their frustrations with the situation, claiming Barca were behind media reports aimed to unsettle the player and increase pressure on Atletico to sell.

Barcelona are wrapping up the signing of Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United and want to make Alvarez their next target as they look to strengthen their front line for next season, with Robert Lewandowski leaving upon the expiration of his contract and Marcus Rashford’s loan coming to an end.

Barca sources say they have already made a €100million offer for Alvarez, and this is reflected in various reports in the Spanish media, but an Atletico source dismissed this as “just another lie” — their language clearly reflecting rising tensions.

That same Atletico source also said the club was “going to have some fun” this afternoon, making it clear they were planning some kind of response to Barca. But few would have expected it to take this form.

Analysis from Spanish football correspondent Dermot Corrigan

Atletico and Barcelona’s tense relationship goes back a few years.

Atletico were angered by Barcelona’s long pursuit of Antoine Griezmann, which saw Griezmann decide to stay in summer 2018 but move to the Camp Nou twelve months later.

In July 2019, Atletico said they would make a complaint to La Liga, claiming Barcelona had underpaid them by €80million in the deal.

Griezmann joined after Barca met a €120million release clause in his contract. Atletico claimed their rivals had negotiated the deal when the Frenchman’s buy-out price was still €200m, but the complaint did not go anywhere.

Griezmann moved between Atletico and Barcelona — and back again (Denis Doyle/Getty Images)There was also awkwardness between the clubs when Griezmann came back to Atletico in 2021, initially in a strange loan deal which led to more strains in the relationships before his permanent return was finalised.

The two teams meeting on the pitch 10 times across different competitions in the last 18 months also brought tensions, particularly during their Champions League quarter-finals in April.

Barca complained about the refereeing when Atletico won the first leg at the Camp Nou, and then denounced the state of the Metropolitano pitch to UEFA ahead of the return.

This provoked annoyance at a high level at Atletico, where everyone enjoyed poking fun at Barca after Simeone’s team progressed in the tie.

A social media post of their home pitch had the caption: “We love the smell of freshly cut grass in the morning.”

Atletico’s social media team have also had a go at city neighbours Real Madrid over the Bernabeu outfit’s regular complaints about Spanish referees in February 2025.

A mocked-up Ikea-style construction manual featured advice to “once again use your TV channel to pressure referees” in “basic instructions” for “derby week”.

Making things even more interesting in the Alvarez situation is the close connection between the two club hierarchies, including Atletico sporting director Mateu Alemany having held that role under Joan Laporta at Barcelona from March 2021, until he resigned in September 2023.
